rv.q: McDonald inhabits the role with such respect for the damaged character she’s playing — not to mention such uncanny vocal transformation — that what could be a fragile construct becomes an immersive drama graced with complex character shadings.
But it’s her extraordinary sensitivity as an actor that makes McDonald’s interpretation memorable.
Lit by her radiance, Lady Day breaks your heart.
It’s Audra McDonald before us now, accepting heartfelt thanks for one of the most exquisite and haunting performances we?re likely to see on stage this year.
But it is her singing that is transcendent.
